name: Why is sewage backing up into my bathtub?

mainEntity.name: Why is sewage backing up into my bathtub?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sewage backing up into your bathtub typically indicates a significant blockage in your main sewer line. This line connects your home's plumbing to the municipal sewer system or a septic tank. Common culprits include tree roots invading pipes, flushed non-biodegradable items like wet wipes or feminine hygiene products, or a build-up of grease and hair over time. Because the bathtub is often the lowest drain point in a bathroom, it's frequently the first fixture to show signs of a main line blockage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sewage backing up into your bathtub usually means there's a serious blockage in your main sewer line, often due to tree roots or accumulated waste.
